previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with shortness of breath, fatigue, and severe anemia (hemoglobin 7.5) following a recent rehabilitation stay after prior hospitalizations for sternal wound infection and C. difficile colitis. She presented with new exertional chest pain, orthopnea, and bilateral leg edema. Workup revealed heart failure exacerbation due to diastolic dysfunction and volume overload, likely compounded by chronic kidney disease. She was transfused two units of packed red blood cells, treated with IV furosemide which was transitioned to oral, and managed for hyperkalemia with kayexalate and dietary modification. Her C. difficile infection was ongoing, so oral vancomycin was continued and a taper plan was established. Blood pressure was optimized with adjustments to metoprolol, hydralazine, and addition of amlodipine. She improved clinically, with resolution of pulmonary edema on imaging, stable renal function, and better exercise tolerance. She was discharged to extended care with a plan for ongoing rehabilitation, medication management, and follow-up with cardiology and nephrology.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year-old woman with extensive cardiac history, 
s/p CABG and multiple re-admissions post-operatively for 
pneumonia, upper gi bleeding, c-difficile colitis and congestive 
heart failure who presents with 2 days of chest pain, found to 
have new RBBB, which is likely secondary to worsening right 
heart failure. During hospitalization patient also with acute on 
chronic renal failure and urinary tract infection.

1. Acute on Chronic Diastolic Heart Failure: Patient with 
peripheral edema and elevated BNP on admission.  Patient was 
initially kept on home dose of lasix.  She received additional 
diureses, first with torsemide and then with IV lasix.  When the 
patient went into renal failure, diuretics were held for three 
days.  The patient's renal function did not improve 
significantly while holding diuretics.  IV lasix was restarted 
and the patient's renal function and shortness of breath 
improved.  The patient was placed on a lasix gtt for one day and 
she continued to improve.  At discharge, patient was 
transitioned to 120 mg PO BID.  The patient will also be 
discharged on amlodipine, imdur, hydralazine, and metoprolol. 

2. Chest pain: Given patient's immobility, chest pain and new 
right bundle branch block on EKG, initially our concern was high 
for a PE. However, VQ scan and CTA did not show PE. Patient with 
troponin at baseline x3. Patient with known diastolic heart 
failure and physical exam evidence of right sided heart failure. 
Reason for new RBBB may be right heart failure secondary to 
worsening diastolic dysfunction. Unlikely pain is related to EKG 
findings. Patient with sternal wound that may also be causing 
pain.  The patient's pain was controlled with percocet and 
gabapentin.  During the hospitalization, she complained of 
substernal chest pain that was relieved with nitroglycerin.  
Again, the patient had no ischemic EKG changes and her troponin 
was at baseline x3.  

3. Urinary Tract Infection: Patient had UA suggestive of UTI in 
ED for which she was started on ciprofloxacin.  The urine 
culture grew out group B strep.  Blood cultures were checked 
which show no growth to date.  The patient spiked fevers and was 
treated with vancomycin (given sternal wound - see below) and 
cefipime for UTI as patient has had many resistant UTIs over the 
past several months.  The patient had a repeat UA/Urine Culture 
the grew proteus.  Her antibiotic regimen was changed to 
Augmentin - 14 day course, she currently has 10 days left of her 
antibiotic course.  The patient will have outpatient urology 
follow-up given her frequent urinary tract infections.    
  
4. Acute on Chronic Renal Failure: On admission, creatinine was 
at patient's baseline of 2.3.  Patient received diuresis with 
both PO and IV lasix as well as PO torsemide.  Patient also 
received contrast for CTA (although she received visipaque and 
was pre-hydrated per radiology protocol).  Five days after 
admission, her creatinine rose - it peaked at 4.2.  Patient was 
seen by renal consult team - differential diagnosis for acute on 
chronic renal failure included AIN given recent cipro use, 
contrast induced nephropathy, or poor forward flow due to CHF.  
Patient's FeUrea suggested a pre-renal etiology of renal 
failure.  Patient's renal function improved with aggressive 
diuresis and was 3.3 at discharge.
    
5. Sternal Wound: The patient has a sternal wound remaining from 
her CABG in ___.  She was evaluated by cardiac surgery, who 
thought her wound looked improved from her last cardiac surgery 
visit.  They recommended wet to dry dressings.  There was a 
pocket of air seen around the ___ sternal wire, but CT surgery 
did not want to remove the wire and wanted to continue 
conservative care.  The wound was cultured and grew MRSA, 
however the wound did not look infected.  The patient was 
treated with IV vancomycin for two days when she spiked a fever, 
but this was discontinued as her fever was likely secondary to 
UTI.  Please continue wet to dry wound dressing changed twice a 
day. 

6. Hypertension:  The antihypertensive regimen was adjusted 
during hospitalization.  We continued her home dose of 
hydralazine.  We decreased her dose of metoprolol to 25 mg BID 
given bradycardia.  We increased her dose of amlodipine to 10 mg 
daily.  We also added imdur 60 mg daily to the patient's 
regimen. 

7. Anemia: Patient with anemia at baseline.  The patient was 
transfuesed one unit PRBC, with slight improvement in HCT of 
24.1 to 26.1. Please consider treatment with epopoetin as 
outpatient given chronic renal insufficiency.  

8. Diabetes Mellitus Type 2: We decreased the patient's dose of 
lantus from 25 to 14 because patient had poor PO intake at 
admission.  We also continued the patient on an insulin sliding 
scale.  At discharge the patient will continue lantus 18 units 
in the morning and an insulin sliding scale.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAM:  Chest frontal and lateral views.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  ___ female with history of chest pain.

___.

FINDINGS:  Single semi-upright portable view of the chest was obtained. 
Patient is rotated slightly to the left.  The patient is status post median
sternotomy and CABG.  Enlargement of the cardiac silhouette persists.  No
focal consolidation, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax is seen.

IMPRESSION:  Persistent cardiomegaly.  Mild pulmonary engorgement.

HISTORY:  ___ female with history of abdominal pain and diarrhea and
history of colitis.

STUDY:  CT of the abdomen and pelvis without contrast; coronal and sagittal
reformatted images were also generated.

COMPARISON:  ___ and ___.

FINDINGS:

ABDOMEN:  Visualized portion of the chest demonstrates calcified
atherosclerotic disease of the coronary arteries.

Within the limits of a non-contrast study, the liver shows no focal lesion. 
The gallbladder shows no stones or wall thickening.  Spleen is normal in size
and appearance.  Pancreas and adrenal glands appear normal.  The kidneys show
no evidence of hydronephrosis or perinephric stranding.  Small and large
intestine show no evidence of obstruction.  Calcified atherosclerotic disease
is noted throughout the abdominal aorta.  There is no free air or free fluid.

PELVIS:  Foley is within the bladder.  Calcified uterine fibroid is noted. 
The rectum appears unremarkable and of a normal wall thickness.

BONES:  No aggressive-appearing lytic or sclerotic lesion is seen.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intra-abdominal process.

HISTORY:  ___ female with left lower extremity swelling.

STUDY:  Left lower extremity venous ultrasound.

FINDINGS:  Grayscale and color Doppler imaging of the bilateral common
femoral, left superficial femoral, left popliteal, and left calf veins was
performed.  There is normal compressibility, flow, and augmentation.

IMPRESSION:  No DVT.

HISTORY:  ___ female with chest pain, new right bundle-branch block. 
Right axis deviation, question PE.  Renal insufficiency thus getting Visipaque
and IV hydration.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT helical acquisition was performed before and after the
uneventful administration of IV contrast through the chest.  5 mm axial
pre-contrast, and 2.5-mm axial post-contrast collimation images as well as a
series reformations, were reviewed.

CT CHEST WITH IV CONTRAST:  Dilution of the IV contrast bolus, large patient
size, and expiratory acquisistion limit the study.  There is no large or
central pulmonary embolus.  There is significant airtrapping, indicative of
small airways disease.  A lower right paratracheal lymph node measuring 0.8 x
1.2 cm, mildly enlarged (4:22).  There is no axillary, or supraclavicular
lymphadenopathy.  There is severe coronary artery disease, cardiomegaly, and
left ventricular hypertrophy.

There has been prior CABG.  Overlying the most inferior (seventh) sternal
wire, an area spanning 1.5 cm demonstrates gas, with soft tissue surrounding
inflammation (4:62).  This was also seen on CT abdomen and pelvis the prior
day, and may represent insulin injection site, less likely to represent
superficial infection.

Osseous structures appear otherwise unremarkable.  The visualized upper
abdomen appears unremarkable except for a small hiatal hernia, as well as an
accessory left hepatic artery arising from the celiac artery.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No large/central pulmonary embolus; markedly limited for detection of
smaller PE.

2.  Significant airtrapping suggests small airways disease, otherwise
parenchymal evaluation limited by expiratory acquisition.

3.  Sternal wires are intact and midline, but superficial to the most inferior
sternal wire, 1.5 cm area of gas with surrounding soft tissue inflammation may
represent injection site of insulin, less likely a site of superficial
infection.

4.  Small hiatal hernia.

5.  CAD, cardiomegaly and left ventricular hypertrophy.

INDICATION:  Acute on chronic renal failure, assess for obstruction.

COMPARISON:  Abdomen/pelvis ultrasound from ___.

FINDINGS:  The right kidney measures 10.2 cm and the left kidney measures 11.1
cm.  There is no evidence of hydronephrosis or obstruction bilaterally.  The
kidneys are otherwise unremarkable in appearance.  The bladder is normal in
appearance.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of hydronephrosis or obstruction.
